newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil issued $13.6 bln debt abroad this yr-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil issued $13.6 bln debt abroad this yr-report.

text.p: Brazil has already surpassed its annual record for capital raised abroad, with a nominal $13.6 billion raised via 193 debt issues, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil said the figures include 25 types of short-, medium- and long-term private and public debt issues.
The country raised $12.9 billion last year, its highest annual record until then, also through the issue of 25 different kinds of debt, the paper said.

Unlike its two main Latin American competitors for foreign capital, Argentina and Mexico, only a small fraction of Brazil's overseas issues -- 3.74 percent -- are federal government debt, Gazeta said.

In Argentina, the central government accounts for 63.58 percent of a total $7.816 billion raised so far this year, while the Mexican government accounts for 44.07 percent of cash raised abroad by that country, it said.
The paper said a high level of foreign reserves and government policy is behind Brazil's low percentage of federal issues.
